justifications.durability: The fence logic now lives in one function that all three doors call, so a future door that forgets it is a visible omission rather than a silent drift; the helper is pure and reads plan.stdin_text with a defined fallback for argv-carried prompts. The new test drives both doors end to end through a stubbed launcher and reads back the exact file the worker would read, asserting the advice, exactly one fence line and the deadline from the pinned attempt start. The declared negative control mutates the shared helper -- the right seam -- and reddens both door cases. Verified green/red by the reviewer.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced at db55c5581: new door test 2 passed EXIT=0; negative control 2 failed EXIT=1 (both doors redden, the CLI door among them); focused five-file gate 35 passed EXIT=0; base four-file arm 33 passed EXIT=0 -- zero added failures. Deductions for the reviewed run's own record: the declared baseline_suite log (base-gate.log) is unreadable (no summary or EXIT=), so completed:true is unsupported by the artifact it names; negative-control.log lacks the required EXIT= terminal line; head-gate.log carries a stale header naming the base revision while running the head tree. The facts are recoverable and were recovered, but the run's evidence is not self-supporting as delivered.
justifications.fit: Reuses the existing structure: both doors already build their plan with resume_plan, and the helper sits beside _spawn in resumption.py and is reused by _resume itself. Docstrings state the mechanism (why the fence must be restated, why a door that writes the bare advice is wrong) rather than history, and no plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in the new code. Naming is mine-neutral.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The goal -- every way of resuming a run writes the attempt's own time fence into the prompt the worker reads -- is met at head. All three advice-file writers route through one helper, so the fence cannot drift between the sweep and the two hand-typed doors. The fence is composed by resume_plan from a fresh _utc_now() at the resume, so the restated deadline is this attempt's own. The base defect was reproduced at both doors before the repair.
justifications.scope_discipline: Only the four declared paths changed; no shared state, plan or index file is touched; dispatch.py is untouched as the brief required. The one edit the brief fenced conditionally -- resumption.py -- is the minimal home for the shared helper, which is the reuse the brief asked for rather than a third copy of the two lines, and it carries no unrelated churn. The remaining deduction is that the manifest states the helper is shared but does not explicitly say why resumption.py had to be edited.
